body:
WHAT
When TEST fails, the message says what is likely wrong. A 401/403 says the endpoint rejected the key (and, once the walk has found the real endpoint, that the URL is right); when no endpoint answered at all the message says no OpenAI-compatible API was found at any known path. The wizard turns a bare 404 status into 'endpoint not found — check the base URL' and the engine's catalog note tells users a model id may need to be fully qualified.

WHY
Gateways authenticate before routing, so a wrong URL and a wrong key both produce 401; blaming the key alone sends users to re-paste a key that was fine.

WHERE
app/main/connection.js — testEndpoint(): authFailure tracking (`the endpoint at ${baseUrl} rejected this API key (HTTP ${status}) — the URL is right, so check the key`), the 'no OpenAI-compatible API found at that address … (tried /v1, /v1/openai, …)' fallback, describeFetchError(err, timeoutMs) for network causes (code/address/port, timeout, self-signed certificate hint). app/renderer/modules/setup.js — describeTestFailure(result) maps 401/403 → 'key rejected by the provider', 404 → 'endpoint not found (404) — check the base URL'.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. When every candidate URL answers 401 on /models, testEndpoint returns status 401 and an error string that names the first rejecting baseUrl and says to check the key.
2. When the as-given URL answers 401 but a later path candidate answers 200, the result is ok:true with baseUrl of the working candidate — the auth failure is remembered but not reported.
3. When a fetch throws with cause.code ECONNREFUSED, the error string contains 'ECONNREFUSED' and the address/port, not a key complaint.
4. When the fetch aborts (AbortError) the error says 'timed out after Ns' and asks whether the server is running.
5. A cause containing SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN appends the 'Allow self-signed certificate' hint; describeTestFailure({status:404}) yields the 'check the base URL' wording.
